items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. However, both companies told Australian parliament last ​month that they would welcome ​laws requiring them to ⁠report data breaches carried out by their AI agents, acknowledging the decision to notify was currently at their discretion.

items.title: Congress’s Permitting Bill Is a ‘Massive Giveaway’ to the AI Data Center Industry, Critics Warn
items.summary: The bill’s advocates argue that its passage would serve as a rare bipartisan win and a victory for affordability. But critics, especially those on the left, are calling for Democrats to wait until the next Congress. “You just heard Americans demand much more of a say in a way that AI is shaping their lives,” says Michele Jawando, the CEO of Omidyar Network. “Whenever you try to ram something through in a lame duck Congress before you have a hundred new House members, that’s never a good look [...] Another major concern from critics is that the bill will lead to many more data centers getting built on federally-owned land. The Trump administration has embraced this idea, and signed an executive order in July 2025 directing the Interior and Energy departments to make federal sites available for data centers and to streamline their environmental reviews. “We’re going to ‘mine, baby, mine’ so we can ‘build, baby, build’ because we’ve got to build AI data centers,” Interior Secretary Doug [...] America’s data center boom has also been a gas boom. In the scramble to bring AI data centers online as fast as possible, many developers have built their own gas power plants instead of waiting to connect to the grid. Global Energy Monitor data reported by Wired show that U.S. gas projects powering data centers increased from roughly 4 gigawatts in early 2024 to 189 gigawatts in development by mid-2026. In some cases, these gas plants have worsened local pollution and exacerbated health issues

items.title: Đưa công nghệ đến gần hơn với người yếu thế
items.summary:
Cán bộ hướng dẫn công dân thao tác trên hệ thống dịch vụ công

Không chỉ hỗ trợ người dân hoàn thành thủ tục, cán bộ, chiến sĩ còn cố gắng sử dụng những cách giải thích đơn giản, dễ hiểu để người dân có thể tự thực hiện trong những lần tiếp theo. Đối với những người gặp khó khăn khi sử dụng công nghệ, cán bộ sẵn sàng hướng dẫn nhiều lần, giải đáp từng thắc mắc với thái độ tận tình, trách nhiệm. [...] Đối với những người thường xuyên sử dụng công nghệ, việc tạo tài khoản dịch vụ công, quét mã QR hoặc tải tài liệu đính kèm có thể thực hiện nhanh chóng. Tuy nhiên, với người cao tuổi và những người ít có điều kiện tiếp xúc với thiết bị điện tử, các thao tác này đôi khi gặp nhiều khó khăn.

Nhận thức được điều đó, cán bộ, chiến sĩ Công an xã Thuận An luôn chú trọng hướng dẫn cụ thể, kiên nhẫn giải thích từng bước để người dân hiểu và thực hiện đúng các thao tác cần thiết. [...] Những hoạt động hỗ trợ tuy giản dị nhưng mang ý nghĩa thiết thực, góp phần giúp người dân thuận lợi hơn trong giải quyết thủ tục hành chính, tiết kiệm thời gian, chi phí đi lại và từng bước nâng cao kỹ năng sử dụng dịch vụ công trực tuyến. Qua đó, Công an xã Thuận An tiếp tục đưa công nghệ đến gần hơn với người dân, nhất là những người còn gặp khó khăn trong tiếp cận công nghệ, để mọi người đều có cơ hội thụ hưởng những tiện ích của chuyển đổi số.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của hàm số $f(x) = x^2$ được tính theo công thức nguyên hàm cơ bản $\int x^n dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$ (với $n \neq -1$).

Áp dụng với $n = 2$:

$$\int x^2 dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

Trong đó, $C$ là hằng số tùy ý.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    # Trường hợp cơ sở (Base cases)
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    
    # Bước đệ quy (Recursive step)
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
n = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {fibonacci(n)}")
```

### Giải thích:
1. **Trường hợp cơ sở (Base case):**
   - Nếu $n \le 0$, hàm trả về `0`.
   - Nếu $n = 1$, hàm trả về `1`.
2. **Bước đệ quy (Recursive step):**
   - Với $n > 1$, hàm tự gọi lại chính nó để tính tổng của 2 số Fibonacci trước đó: `fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)`.

---

### Lưu ý về hiệu năng:
Cách tính đệ quy thuần túy này có độ phức tạp thời gian là $O(2^n)$, sẽ rất chậm khi $n$ lớn. Để tối ưu hóa khi $n$ lớn, bạn có thể sử dụng thêm kỹ thuật ghi nhớ (**Memoization**) với `@functools.lru_cache`:

```python
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fibonacci_memo(n):
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci_memo(n - 1) + fibonacci_memo(n - 2)

# Chạy nhanh kể cả với n lớn
print(fibonacci_memo(50))  # Kết quả: 12586269025
```

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
